name: Security Engineering
description: A secure IT application requires both presence of desired security features, like access control, and absence of undesired security flaws, like software vulnerabilities to hackers. After discussing basic terms like security versus safety and security goals, we first investigate the engineering process for security critical applications. Here the documents provided by the BSI are valuable companions. From an initial security requirements analysis we progress to the vulnerability and risk assessment, which includes economical aspects. We learn how to define a security policy and specify its reflection in the security architecture. We look at basic security mechanisms and get familiar with classical access and information flow control models. We address methods for validation and assessment of secure applications, like penetration tests, formal methods and the valuation according to Common Criteria. We finish part one with concepts for IT security management and tools for intrusion detection and prevention. In part two we deal with secure software development. We address basic attack vectors of hackers, crackers and malware authors. We refresh our assembler and memory management skills and learn about shell code. We see how insecure programming among other things facilitates buffer and integer overflow vulnerabilities, script injection, and cross-site-scripting. We learn how to look for such vulnerabilities systematically with the help of tools, social engineering, fuzzing, and debugging. We investigate professional handling of security incidents, patch processes and the work of Computer Emergency Response Teams (CERTs). We address principles of secure software design and secure coding, as well as related testing methods, including hostile environments and side channel attacks. We look at the Microsoft Security Development Cycle.
